policy.userAgentNote: Generic product token so the channel name is not sent to third parties unless the owner opts in: set RADAR_USER_AGENT or --user-agent (for example 'ZooraNewsRadar/0.1').
policy.alsoObeyRobotsNote: The radar's output feeds an AI-assisted drafting step, so a source is skipped when its robots.txt disallows the path for Anthropic's user-directed agent token as well as for our own token.
policy.storage: Titles, URLs, dates and excerpts of at most 280 characters only. No article bodies are stored, in the cache or in the output.

tiers.A: Primary statements (the project's own report or post-mortem, law-enforcement or regulator releases), security-firm research and post-mortems. One unhedged tier-A source that is not an incident database confirms an incident.
tiers.B: Established news outlets. Two unhedged tier-B outlets that do not relay the same origin (the same firm's research, the same report) confirm an incident; one that relays the project's own statement does too.
tiers.C: Aggregators and mixed sponsored/original sites. Never count toward confirmation.
tiers.tracker: Incident databases ("tracker": true; tier A for figures and dates): they seed, date and size an incident but never confirm it alone. A record whose only reference is an X post is marked unverified.

lanes.crypto: Crypto security: an item needs crypto context and an incident term or a security topic (README, How a brief is built).
lanes.ai: AI security: an item needs AI context (an LLM, a chatbot, an AI agent or coding agent, an MCP server, model weights, a deepfake or cloned voice, a named AI product) AND an AI-security incident or topic (prompt injection, a jailbreak, data or secrets exposed through an AI tool, a malicious or poisoned model, package, extension or MCP server, an AI-assisted intrusion, deepfake or voice-clone fraud, AI-generated phishing, AI-washing charges). Vendor marketing, product launches, deals, funding, webinars and opinion never count.
lanes.both: A source in both lanes keeps an item that passes either rule. An item or incident that passes both rules is in lane "both".

sources.name: DefiLlama
sources.terms: Public JSON API, no key. robots.txt: 404 (no rules). The structured backbone: one record per incident (fields documented in README). The `source` field was empty for all 1,375 records on 2026-11-24, so records link to the API URL with a #name@date fragment. Attribute figures as 'DefiLlama'. API terms not re-read in this session (defillama.com is not reachable here).

sources.name: SlowMist Hacked
sources.terms: Security firm's incident database, first index page only (20 newest cases). robots.txt: 404 (no rules). Footer: 'Copyright SlowMist Hacked All Rights Reserved'. Store target, date, figure, attack method and a 280-character excerpt with attribution. The per-case reference link (mostly x.com) is recorded as cited by SlowMist and never fetched.

sources.name: rekt.news
sources.terms: Post-mortem publication, home page only (12 newest posts). robots.txt disallows /api only. Footer: 'all content copyright rekt, all rights reserved'. Title, link and the index excerpt (at most 280 characters), attributed. Only '<Protocol> - Rekt' posts form incidents; essays are listed as unclustered.

sources.name: Chainalysis
sources.terms: Blockchain-analytics firm's research blog (WordPress RSS). robots.txt blocks only /wp-content/uploads for *. Headline, link and the feed summary (at most 280 characters), attributed to Chainalysis. Promotional posts are excluded.

sources.name: CertiK
sources.terms: Security firm's blog index (server-rendered cards with dates). robots.txt disallows /api/ only and allows Claude-User. Card title, link and card summary (at most 280 characters). Case studies and announcements are excluded as promotional.

sources.name: TRM Labs
sources.terms: Blockchain-intelligence firm's blog index (server-rendered cards). robots.txt: Allow / for * and explicitly for Claude-User. Card title, link and summary (at most 280 characters).

sources.name: CoinDesk
sources.terms: Public RSS. robots.txt allows * on this path; it disallows named AI crawlers (ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web, GPTBot and others) everywhere except /price/, but sets no rule for Claude-User. The radar reads only this feed, never article pages, and keeps headline, link and the feed description (at most 280 characters) with attribution. Feed copyright: CoinDesk.

sources.name: Decrypt
sources.terms: Public RSS. robots.txt: no disallow rules for *. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: Cointelegraph
sources.terms: Public RSS. robots.txt disallows URLs with tracking parameters; the radar strips utm_* from stored links and never fetches article pages. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: The Block
sources.terms: Public RSS. robots.txt: /rss.xml not disallowed; Content-Signal search=yes, ai-input=yes. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed. Copyright The Block.

sources.name: The Defiant
sources.terms: Public RSS (100 items). robots.txt allows / for * (disallows python-requests, which the radar does not use). The /frontier/ section is AI and tech news and is excluded. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: DL News
sources.terms: Public RSS (Arc). robots.txt: Allow / for *. The feed mixes new and months-old items; dates decide what counts. The feed's analytics <script> element is ignored, never run. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: Blockworks
sources.terms: UNVERIFIED: blockworks.co was refused by this session's network proxy on 2026-11-24, so neither the feed path nor robots.txt could be checked. The run reports it as skipped until the host is reachable; then verify the path.

sources.name: Web3 is Going Just Great
sources.terms: Atom feed, CC BY-SA 3.0 (feed <rights>): attribution required. robots.txt allows all. Entry timestamps can be catch-up times, not event times, so freshness uses the earliest date stated in the entry. Commentary-heavy aggregator: tier C, never confirms.

sources.name: crypto.news
sources.terms: Public RSS. robots.txt disallows ?utm_ and similar parameters (not used). Mixes original reporting with sponsored and price content, so it is tier C. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: Coin Edition
sources.terms: Public RSS (10 items). robots.txt (Yoast) blocks admin and search paths only. Smaller outlet with market and sponsored content: tier C. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: Unit 42
sources.terms: Palo Alto Networks' threat research blog (WordPress RSS, the 15 newest posts with full text). robots.txt disallows /wp-admin/ only. Headline, link and the feed summary (at most 280 characters, without the 'The post ... appeared first on' footer), attributed to Unit 42. It covers AI-agent attacks and crypto drainers, so it carries both lanes. Promotional posts are excluded (vendor-blog rule), and so are the 'Threat Intelligence Highlights' digests (round-ups of earlier posts).

sources.name: Microsoft Security Blog
sources.terms: Microsoft's security blog (WordPress RSS, the 10 newest posts with full text): Microsoft Threat Intelligence and AI Red Team research. robots.txt allows the feed path for * (it disallows query-string and store paths only). Headline, link and summary (at most 280 characters, without the WordPress footer), attributed to Microsoft Security. Product, award and analyst-ranking posts are excluded as promotional.

sources.name: Embrace The Red
sources.terms: A security researcher's blog (Hugo RSS listing every post; the radar reads 200 at most): primary AI-agent exploit and prompt-injection research, usually published once the vendor has fixed the issue. Low volume. robots.txt: Allow / for *. Headline, link and summary (at most 280 characters), attributed to Embrace The Red, never to a person. Concept-level labels only: no payload, prompt or step is ever stored or repeated.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.terms: Public RSS (the 15 newest items). robots.txt: Crawl-delay 1 and no rule for this path for *; it disallows ClaudeBot but sets no rule for Claude-User. Sponsored posts (author line 'Sponsored by ...': the radar reads that flag and never stores author names) and deals are excluded. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: The Record
sources.terms: Recorded Future News, public RSS (the 5 newest items). robots.txt answered 404 on 2026-11-24 (no rules). Podcast episodes are excluded. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed to The Record.

sources.name: SecurityWeek
sources.terms: Public RSS (the main feed, 10 newest items). The AI-category feed is behind a Cloudflare challenge and is not used. robots.txt allows / for * but disallows URLs with query strings (stored links carry none). Funding, M&A, people moves, webinars, virtual events and the 'In Other News' round-up are excluded. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters, without the 'appeared first on SecurityWeek' footer), attributed.

sources.name: Dark Reading
sources.terms: Public RSS (the 50 newest items). robots.txt disallows ClaudeBot, GPTBot and other named AI crawlers everywhere but sets no rule for Claude-User, so its * group applies (the feed is allowed). Wire press releases carry no author line in the feed and are excluded (the radar reads only whether a byline exists, never the name; the check switches itself off with a warning if most items lack one); careers, events, partner content and the editors' video round-ups are excluded too. Headline, link and description (at most 280 characters), attributed.

sources.name: KrebsOnSecurity
sources.terms: Investigative security journalism (WordPress RSS, the 10 newest posts with full text). robots.txt sets Crawl-delay 35 for *, which the radar obeys, and does not disallow /feed/. Its category tags name people, so the radar keeps no categories from this feed (nothing to cache). Headline, link and the feed summary (at most 280 characters), attributed to KrebsOnSecurity.

sources.name: AI Incident Database
sources.terms: The Responsible AI Collaborative's incident database (Gatsby RSS, the 100 newest reports; about a third are AI security). Each item is a report from ANOTHER outlet: its link is the original article, and its description ends with the database's citation link (incidentdatabase.ai/cite/<incident>#<report>), which the radar keeps as the report's incident reference (reports with the same one are grouped) and never fetches. Discovery only, like Web3 is Going Just Great: tier C, never confirms, and every fact must come from the original report it links. robots.txt answered 404 on 2026-11-24 (no rules). Its dates are when a report was added, so freshness uses the earliest date the text states.
